comment: The numbers and words of geometric pricing (src/geometric-pricing.mjs). A price rule is one record any offer can carry; its `mode` picks how the price moves by multiplication instead of by opinion. `ladder` lays prices a fixed ratio apart so a price test covers a wide range with few arms and each round can zoom in. `controller` is a variable speed controller: the price doubles over `sales_to_double` sales and each person who reached the price and did not buy takes a little off, so it holds still at `target_win_rate`. `bracket` is his bracketed price search: the highest price someone accepted is L, the lowest price above it that was refused is U, and the next quote is the geometric middle, the square root of L times U, until they meet. Every default below is only used when a rule leaves a field out.

words.no_rule: {label} has no price rule: save it with a rule to use it.
words.no_rounds: A {mode} rule has no next round; its price is read with price_now.
words.controller: The price the rule gives now is {price}: {sales} sales among {reached} people who reached it.
words.bracket_open: No price has been tried yet, so the first price is {price}.
words.bracket_all_refused: Nobody has bought yet, so the next price is {price}, a step down from the lowest refused price.
words.bracket_climb: {low} was bought and nothing higher has been refused, so the next price is {price}.
words.bracket_between: {low} was bought and {high} was refused, so the next price is the geometric middle, {price}.
words.bracket_met: {low} was bought and {high} was refused, and they are close enough: the price is {price}.
words.not_running: {label} is {state}, so it has no next round.
words.round_held: {label} has settled on {price}; there is no next round.
words.offers_need_owner: {label} tests offers with their own payment links, so a new price in it goes through whoever sets those offers: add the offer priced {price} first.
